analysis.investment_thesis: At P/E 44x and P/B 6.93x, Park Medi World trades at nearly 4x its Graham Number of approximately INR 55 — there is no margin of safety whatsoever. The speculative premium demands flawless execution of a growth story, precisely the kind of bet a disciplined investor must refuse.
key_strengths: 5 consecutive years of positive earnings (187→213 Cr net profit), satisfying minimum earnings continuity
Revenue growing at 16.1% CAGR with operating margins holding near 20-27% range, demonstrating some competitive position in healthcare
Equity base expanding rapidly (275→1,201 Cr), reducing reliance on external capital over time
key_risks: P/E of 44x and P/B of 6.93x catastrophically violate Graham's limits of 15x and 1.5x — paying 4x liquidation value
Finance costs compounding at 26.3% CAGR (24→61 Cr); borrowings rose from 292 to 734 Cr — debt burden accelerating faster than earnings
Net profit CAGR of only 3.3% (2021–2025) versus revenue CAGR of 16.1% — severe margin dilution; earnings also fell sharply in 2024 (152 Cr vs 228 Cr prior year)
red_flags: Graham Number ~INR 55 vs market price INR 216 — stock must fall ~75% to reach intrinsic value
No dividend mentioned — shareholders receive no tangible return while paying a luxury price
Free cash flow highly volatile (86, 64, 106, 294, 66 Cr) with 2025 FCF collapsing to 66 Cr despite record revenue — capex jumped to 159 Cr suggesting capital intensity is rising
analysis.detailed_analysis:
By every quantitative filter I have ever devised, Park Medi World is priced for speculation, not investment. The Graham Number — the ceiling price combining earnings power and book value — computes to approximately INR 55 (using EPS ~4.9 and BVPS ~27.7). The market demands INR 216, a 3.9x premium. A P/E of 44x and P/B of 6.93x are not minor violations; they are the hallmark of a popularity contest, not rational valuation. Mr. Market is in an exuberant mood about Indian healthcare, and the intelligent investor must refuse to participate at these prices regardless of the story being told.

The business itself is not without merit — five years of unbroken profits and respectable operating margins of ~20% suggest a functioning enterprise with some local competitive position. However, the financials show worrying trends beneath the surface: finance costs have grown at 26.3% CAGR as borrowings ballooned from INR 292 Cr to INR 734 Cr, and net profit grew a meager 3.3% CAGR over four years while revenue doubled. The 2024 collapse in net profit to INR 152 Cr from INR 228 Cr — a 33% drop — illustrates precisely the earnings vulnerability that demands a margin of safety. There is none here at current prices. I would require a price below INR 60 before even beginning to consider this security.
